papers.title: CrossMol: Cross-Modal Mask-Predict Pre-training For 3D Molecular Data
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Self-supervised pre-training models for molecular data have demonstrated notable results across many downstream tasks. The inherent multimodal properties of molecules have also motivated efforts to capture information from different modalities. However, current multimodal molecular pre-training models usually treat these modalities as equal and independent, despite differences in their information content. Three-dimensional (3D) molecular structures generally contain finer-grained information than the simplified molecular-input line-entry system (SMILES), which primarily captures higher-level semantic information, such as molecular topology. Results We designed a cross-modal mask-predict pre-training model, Cross Mol , to capture semantic associations between modalities with unequal information volumes. The model completes missing 3D structure using higher-level semantic information from another modality, such as SMILES. This allows it to learn cross-modal associations and better understand fine-grained 3D structural information. We also introduce a reweighted distance prediction loss to improve the modelling of short-range structural information. Experiments show that Cross Mol achieves large performance gains on multiple downstream molecular tasks, attaining state-of-the-art results. Availability and Implementation The source code and training data are available at https://github.com/zhengkangjie/crossmol . The code is archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19653204
papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Self-supervised pre-training models for molecular data have demonstrated notable results across many downstream tasks. The inherent multimodal properties of molecules have also motivated efforts to capture information from different modalities. However, current multimodal molecular pre-training models usually treat these modalities as equal and independent, despite differences in their information content. Three-dimensional (3D) molecular structures generally contain finer-grained information than the simplified molecular-input line-entry system (SMILES), which primarily captures higher-level semantic information, such as molecular topology.

RESULTS: We designed a cross-modal mask-predict pre-training model, CrossMol, to capture semantic associations between modalities with unequal information volumes. The model completes missing 3D structure using higher-level semantic information from another modality, such as SMILES. This allows it to learn cross-modal associations and better understand fine-grained 3D structural information. We also introduce a reweighted distance prediction loss to improve the modelling of short-range structural information. Experiments show that CrossMol achieves large performance gains on multiple downstream molecular tasks, attaining state-of-the-art results.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code and training data are available at https://github.com/zhengkangjie/crossmol. The code is archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19653204.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary material contains the task-specific hyperparameters.

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
针对分子数据设计的自监督预训练模型在众多下游任务中取得了显著成果。由于分子本身具有多模态特性，人们也致力于从不同模态中提取有价值的信息。然而现有的多模态分子预训练模型通常将这些模态视为等同且独立的，尽管它们在信息含量上存在差异。三维分子结构通常包含比简化分子输入格式（如SMILES）更详细的信息，后者主要捕捉分子拓扑等高层次的语义特征。  

**研究方法**  
我们设计了一种跨模态掩码预测预训练模型Cross Mol，旨在捕捉那些信息量不同的模态之间的语义关联。该模型能够利用另一种模态中的高级语义信息来补全缺失的三维结构数据，从而帮助学习跨模态的关联规律并更深入地理解三维结构细节。此外，我们还引入了加权距离预测损失函数，以更好地模拟分子结构中的短程相互作用。  

**实验结果**  
实验表明，Cross Mol在多种下游分子任务中均取得了显著的性能提升，其效果已达到当前研究的最高水平。  

**代码与数据资源**  
源代码及训练数据可访问以下链接：https://github.com/zhengkangjie/crossmol。相关代码已被存档于DOI数据库：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19653204。

**结果**：我们设计了一种跨模态掩码预测预训练模型CrossMol，旨在捕捉那些信息量不均衡的模态之间的语义关联。该模型能够利用另一种模态中的高级语义信息来补充缺失的三维结构数据，从而帮助学习跨模态之间的联系，并更深入地理解精细的三维结构信息。我们还引入了一种加权距离预测损失函数，以更好地模拟分子短程结构特征。实验结果表明，CrossMol在多种下游分子任务中均取得了显著的性能提升，其结果已达到当前研究的最高水平。

**可用性与实现方式**：源代码及训练数据可访问以下链接：https://github.com/zhengkangjie/crossmol。代码存档地址为：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19653204。

**补充信息**：补充材料中包含了针对具体任务所设定的超参数配置。
